title: HTTP fails while ping and DNS still work
scenario: PC-A and SRV1 share a working VLAN and IPv4 subnet. A fresh HTTP request fails. The technician collects the following client and server observations; they are representative teaching evidence.

exhibits.title: PC-A test results
exhibits.text:
ping 192.168.40.20: replies received
nslookup www.lab.test: returns 192.168.40.20
Fresh request to http://192.168.40.20: fails
Fresh request to http://www.lab.test: fails

exhibits.title: SRV1 Services settings
exhibits.text:
HTTP: Off
DNS: On
A record www.lab.test: 192.168.40.20

question: Which diagnosis is directly supported by all the evidence?
options: The client needs a different default gateway for the HTTP service.
The name record points to a different host from the approved server.
The HTTP service is disabled while the other tested services still work.
A failed TCP opening is impossible because the ICMP round trip succeeds.
explanation: The server setting explicitly identifies HTTP Off, while the fresh lookup returns the approved address and ICMP replies. An incorrect gateway is not needed for this same-subnet exchange, and successful ICMP does not establish a TCP opening. Without the server-setting exhibit, the failed-browser symptom alone would not identify one cause.
fix: On SRV1, open Services → HTTP and set HTTP On. Start fresh requests to both http://192.168.40.20 and http://www.lab.test, verify that the page loads, then save the restored Packet Tracer topology. Do not change addressing or routing to repair a deliberately stopped service.

title: The server address works but its name does not
scenario: The isolated LAN contains PC-A at 192.168.40.10/24 and SRV1 at 192.168.40.20/24. No device uses 192.168.40.99. HTTP and DNS are enabled on SRV1, and its www.lab.test A record correctly points to 192.168.40.20. The technician checks a fresh browser request and the PC configuration.

exhibits.title: PC-A configured settings
exhibits.text:
IPv4 address: 192.168.40.10
Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0
DNS server: 192.168.40.99

exhibits.title: Observed tests
exhibits.text:
http://192.168.40.20: page loads
nslookup www.lab.test using configured DNS: fails
http://www.lab.test: name cannot be resolved

question: Which correction addresses the demonstrated cause?
options: Set PC-A’s DNS server to 192.168.40.20 and repeat the fresh lookup.
Replace the server’s correct A record with a pointer to 192.168.40.99.
Change SRV1’s HTTP port to 53 so that the browser can request the name.
Set a default gateway on PC-A before attempting its on-link DNS server.
explanation: The client sends name queries to an explicitly unused address, while direct-IP HTTP already works. Correct the selected resolver, then requery and repeat the original named request. Changing the valid A record or the HTTP port confuses separate services; a default gateway does not make the unused on-link resolver exist.
fix: Open PC-A Desktop → IP Configuration, change DNS Server to 192.168.40.20, and run nslookup www.lab.test. Confirm the returned address, open http://www.lab.test, and save the repaired topology. Leave the working server IP, subnet mask, and HTTP service unchanged.
